title: Reading or Remembering? Measuring Temporal Contamination in Language Models
abstract: arXiv:2611.21554v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Language models are now used to read central-bank text for economic forecasting, but most were trained on text written after the documents they read. A model reading a 2021 FOMC statement may already know that inflation rose in 2022, so part of its apparent skill can be memory of the outcome, a temporal form of test-set contamination. We measure this memory on FOMC statements and minutes from 2000 to 2026 by comparing modern open models with chronologically consistent models, which are trained only on text from before a fixed date. Asked about past GDP outcomes given only a date, models that cannot know the answer still reach an AUC of up to 0.64 from priors on dates and eras, so chance is the wrong baseline. Against these memory-free models on the same questions, most modern models recall which years had strong growth. Membership-inference scores sort documents by era and document type rather than by whether a model saw them, as exact

translated_title: 阅读还是记忆？测量语言模型中的时间污染
translated_abstract: 语言模型如今被用于阅读央行文本以进行经济预测，但大多数模型的训练文本写于其所阅读文档之后。一个阅读2021年FOMC声明的模型可能已经知道2022年通胀上升，因此其表面上的部分能力可能只是对结果的记忆——这是测试集污染的一种时间性形式。我们在2000年至2026年的FOMC声明和会议纪要上测量这种记忆，方法是将现代开源模型与时间上一致的模型（即仅在固定日期之前的文本上训练的模型）进行比较。当仅给定日期询问过去的GDP结果时，无法知晓答案的模型仅凭对日期和年代的先验仍能达到高达0.64的AUC，因此随机水平是错误的基线。在相同问题上与这些无记忆模型相比，大多数现代模型能回忆起哪些年份有强劲增长。成员推断分数是按时代和文档类型对文档进行排序，而非按模型是否见过它们来排序……
tldr: 论文发现语言模型在基于央行文本进行经济预测时，其表现可能部分源于对“未来”结果的记忆（时间性测试集污染），并通过与仅使用过去数据训练的无记忆模型对比，证明现代模型确实能回忆起未来的经济结果，且传统的随机基线并不适用于评估这种污染。
en_tdlr: This paper reveals that language models' apparent skill in economic forecasting from central-bank text may partly stem from memorizing future outcomes—a temporal form of test-set contamination—and shows by comparing with chronologically consistent memory-free models that modern models indeed recall future economic results, while chance is the wrong baseline.
